route: iPad Air 11-inch (M4) Simulator, iOS 26.5, portrait. Offline LAN host, Katabatic CTF, two bots, audio on, untouched default observer view. No build, debugger, sampler or screen recording during the listed windows; the user desktop was active (load average 4.2-6.0).
measurement: Opt-in TRIBES_FRAME_TIMING=1 native swap logger (gl4es_context.c): 30-second windows of SDL_GL_SwapWindow submissions. Measures CPU-side frame submission, not GPU completion or display.

rejected_candidate.change: Compiler-inlined permission checks for later accesses in existing 16-access groups (docs/experiments/inline-grouped-guard-rejected.patch)
rejected_candidate.component_tests: Grouped-access runtime test: 6 inline-check faults abort before access; ThreadSanitizer clean; microbenchmark 3.2x faster per access. Not reflected in the game.

profile.tool: macOS sample, 10 s, after timing windows

conclusion: Steady observer view runs at 6.0-7.0 FPS across two runs of the same source (mean 6.75 and 6.2): run-to-run variation is about 8% on this shared Mac. Swap submission is 0.04 ms, so the game thread is CPU-bound. The rejected candidate (6.0-6.3 FPS) is within that variation: no measurable whole-game change, while code size nearly doubled. Per-check cost (~8.5 ns: two calls, two TLS lookups, checks) times ~12M checked guest accesses per frame bounds this design well below 30 FPS.
window_selection: Steady observer view only: excludes the match-start transition, the profiler window and windows overlapping other local work.

restored_source_rerun.source: d73c01c runtime + frame-timing logger, rebuilt after the experiments (same source as baseline)
restored_source_rerun.identity_note: Same source and size as the baseline binary c99ee37b, but not byte-identical; the cause was not isolated. Functionally exercised on the same route (console-started host, two bots).
